description: We are Sara, Judy, Rosal, Ahmed, Ammar, and Moamen, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: “Abandoned but not Forgotten.” Judy is our Team Leader. Ammar and Moamen are Developers. Ahmed is our Researcher. Sara and Rosal are our Artists, responsible for the visual design. Together, we combine leadership, development, research, and creativity to explore abandoned space equipment on the Moon and Mars.
summary:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an interactive educational web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It celebrates humanity's robotic pioneers by allowing users to explore 12 historic spacecraft left behind across the Moon and Mars.
Built with React, Vite, and Three.js, the application combines immersive 3D planetary environments, orbital visualizations, and interactive spacecraft inspections with technical information and historical mission records.
It features two exploration modes: a story-driven campaign guided by Luna, featuring cinematic storytelling and educational quizzes, and an unrestricted Arcade Mode. Additional features include English and Arabic localization, persistent progression, procedural audio, responsive mobile interfaces, and optimized 3D assets.
The project transforms space exploration history into an engaging experience, ensuring that even after these spacecraft have stopped operating, their scientific contributions are never forgotten
details:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten

NASA Space Apps Challenge Project

An interactive 3D exploration experience built around one idea: just because a spacecraft stopped operating doesn't mean its story should end there.

Our team wanted to build something more interesting than a regular website displaying spacecraft information. So we combined 3D exploration, visual-novel storytelling, and educational content into one experience.

What does it actually do?

The application lets users explore 12 historic spacecraft across the Moon and Mars, including the Apollo Lunar Rover, Opportunity, Ingenuity, Viking 1, LRO, and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

There are two main exploration modes:

  • Story Mode: A narrative-driven experience featuring Luna, with cinematic scenes, dialogue, educational missions, and progressive spacecraft unlocking.
  • Arcade Mode: No progression restrictions. Just jump in and explore all 12 spacecraft.

What went into building it?

As the programmer on the team, I handled the application's development and the integration of its different systems.

Some of the main technologies and implementations include:

  • React + Vite: Application architecture, component management, and UI.
  • Three.js: Interactive 3D planetary environments, surface exploration, orbital views, and spacecraft inspection.
  • SVG + 3D Projection: Dynamic telemetry leader lines connecting spacecraft components to their technical descriptions.
  • Web Audio API: Procedural sound effects, environmental ambience, and audio management.
  • LocalStorage: Persistent campaign progression and spacecraft unlocking.
  • Localization: English and Arabic support, including RTL layouts.
  • Performance Optimization: Draco compression, WebP textures, model caching, and responsive camera positioning.

Other Features

  • Interactive spacecraft component inspection.
  • Technical dossiers and educational quizzes.
  • Lunar and Martian surface environments.
  • Orbital views with planetary bodies and satellite trajectories.
  • Cinematic storytelling and character reactions.
  • Responsive desktop and mobile interfaces.
  • Audio, graphics, and language settings.

A little about the process

This project involved a lot more than putting 3D models on a webpage. Getting the models, camera positioning, UI, telemetry pointers, audio, and progression systems to work together was a challenge of its own.

Some things worked immediately. Others... not so much.

There was plenty of debugging, experimenting, and refining along the way, but the goal was always to build a complete interactive experience rather than another static archive.

And that's what our team set out to accomplish.

These spacecraft may be abandoned, but they are definitely not forgotten.
